docs.title: strands-phone
docs.text:
Call your agent.

A real phone number that rings a Strands BidiAgent. It listens and speaks at the same time, can be interrupted, calls tools and hangs up when you're done. It runs on Nova 2 Sonic or gpt-realtime-2.

Quickstart How it works

answer calls
infra/up.sh        # number, Voice Connector, EC2, role
deploy/deploy.sh   # systemd: strands-phone answer
# now dial the number in .state.env
place a call
strands-phone call +15551234567
# the agent speaks first, then listens
the agent on the line
BidiAgent(
    model=make_model(),  # nova | openai
    tools=[current_time, hang_up],
    system_prompt="You are on a real phone call...",
)
measured, first real call
answered: 31 ms
first_audio: 0.82 s
reply_after_you: 0.13 to 0.68 s
tool_call: current_time
ended_by: hang_up

docs.title: Design
docs.text: A SIP trunk carries audio in both directions. Chime SDK Voice Connector owns the number and the trunk. Origination sends incoming calls to the host, and termination accepts outgoing calls only from the host's Elastic IP. One EC2 host runs strands-phone.service: InboundCall answers, Call dials, and both bridge RTP to a BidiAgent.

docs.title: Choices
docs.text:
• No SDK change. The bridge sends one agent.send(AudioDelta) per RTP packet in, and feeds agent.receive() into a playout buffer on the way out.
  • The phone's own rate. Nova 2 Sonic runs at 8 kHz in and out. Only 24 kHz models pay for Up3 / Down3.
  • One call per process. systemd restarts the listener after every call, so no state leaks from one call to the next.
  • Open the model while the phone rings. The agent is ready the moment the call is answered.
  • Never digitally silent. The model only answers while audio flows, so the clock sends a -60 dBFS noise floor whenever the buffer is empty.
  • Evidence for every call. A stereo WAV plus a JSON timeline. Measure barge-in from the WAV.
  • No long-lived AWS secrets on the host. Nova signs with the instance role. An OpenAI key stays in a root-only file.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
1. Register a caller name (CNAM), so mobile carriers stop sending outbound calls to voicemail.
  2. Measure barge-in from the WAV, with a target under 300 ms, using a scripted SIP test caller.
  3. Hand a call to a human or a contact-centre queue.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
strands-phone is a small SIP user agent. Chime SDK Voice Connector handles the phone network. strands-phone speaks SIP over UDP for signalling and RTP with G.711 u-law for audio. On an incoming INVITE it replies 100 Trying, then 180 Ringing, then 200 OK. As InboundCall it answers calls; as Call it places them. The model connection opens while the line is still ringing, so the agent is ready the moment the call is picked up.

Each RTP packet is decoded to PCM16 and becomes one AudioDelta sent to the agent. The agent's bidi_audio_delta events fill a playout buffer, and a 20 ms clock sends one frame per tick. When the buffer is empty, the clock sends a -60 dBFS noise floor instead of silence. When the caller interrupts, the model emits bidi_barge_in and the buffer is dropped, so the agent stops mid-word.

File strands_phone/sip.py parse, SDP, the datagram endpoint strands_phone/rtp.py, g711.py RTP PCMU, u-law identical to audioop bit for bit strands_phone/resample.py Up3 / Down3, a 31-tap FIR for 24 kHz models strands_phone/call.py Call, InboundCall, the clock, barge-in, opt-in recording strands_phone/agent.py make_model(), BidiAgent, current_time, hang_up

The tests include a loopback call: our Call dials our InboundCall over real SIP and RTP on localhost, and audio has to cross in both directions.

docs.title: Models
docs.text:
MODEL_PROVIDER Model Rate on the line Auth nova Amazon Nova 2 Sonic 8 kHz in and out, no resampling EC2 instance role openai OpenAI gpt-realtime-2 24 kHz, Up3 / Down3 in the bridge OPENAI_API_KEY

Credentials never expire: the role rotates itself and signs with SigV4, and the OpenAI key sits in a root-only file. Nova's role needs bedrock:InvokeModel on InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream; OpenAI's key goes as Authorization: Bearer. Both models get the same tools and the same prompt. To switch, change one line in .secrets.env and run deploy/deploy.sh again.

Measured over the phone network:

Nova 2 Sonic gpt-realtime-2 answered 31 ms 312 ms (websocket opens while ringing) greeting audio after answer 0.82 s 0.62 s tool call yes yes

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: You need an AWS account with Chime SDK Voice and Bedrock (Nova 2 Sonic), the AWS CLI, and Python 3.12. It takes about five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Provision
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/cagataycali/strands-phone && cd strands-phone
infra/up.sh --state NJ

This orders a local number and creates a Voice Connector, a t4g.small EC2 instance with an Elastic IP, a security group and the instance role. It writes the ids to .state.env. Running it again changes nothing that already exists. These resources cost money while they sit idle.

docs.title: 2. Deploy
docs.text:
deploy/deploy.sh

This copies the repo to the host, installs it, and starts the strands-phone systemd service. The service answers one call at a time and starts listening again as soon as a call ends.

docs.title: 3. Call it
docs.text:
Dial the NUMBER from .state.env. To have the agent dial out instead, run this on the host:

set -a; . /etc/strands-phone.env; set +a
~/venv/bin/strands-phone call +15551234567

With RECORD_CALLS=1, every call leaves calls/<utc>.wav (left channel: the other party, right channel: the agent) and a .json timeline.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
Variable Default MODEL_PROVIDER nova nova or openai NOVA_MODEL amazon.nova-2-sonic-v1:0 OPENAI_MODEL gpt-realtime-2 needs OPENAI_API_KEY VOICE matthew / marin per provider MAX_CALL_S 600 hard stop RECORD_CALLS off 1 keeps calls/<utc>.wav + .json; check consent laws first SIP_ALLOW Chime CIDRs comma-separated sources that may send SIP; empty accepts all OWNER_NAME, SYSTEM_PROMPT none whose line it is; or replace the whole prompt TIMEZONE UTC for the current_time tool VC_HOST, CALLER_ID, PUBLIC_IP from .state.env written by deploy.sh

Put secrets in .secrets.env. Git ignores it, and deploy.sh copies it into the host's root-only /etc/strands-phone.env.

docs.title: Tear down
docs.text: infra/down.sh   # asks first, then deletes everything and releases the number
